newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. denies it issued report on Algerian elections.
newsitem.headline: U.N. denies it issued report on Algerian elections.

text.p: The United Nations on Monday denied it issued a report, printed in Algerian newspapers, that criticised Algerian election procedures in which pro-government parties swept to a majority in the new parliament.

U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard told reporters that a statement was issued by international observers who were not under U.N. control and that U.N. officials were surprised it had been attributed to the world organisation.

"The United Nations has no role on assessing the validity of the elections," Eckhard said. "We have a small group of four people who were consultants. There was an international group of election monitors not under U.N. authority and it was those people who issued a communique today."
In the report, the observers said there had been problems moving freely during monitoring the poll, and there were questions over voting by security forces.

The statement published by two local newspapers said: "While observers were able to move without fear or threats, several had difficulties to carry out their work with all the independence and free movement necessary to assess objectively these elections."
The statement said the observers also questioned what happened in the special voting buros, where security forces cast their ballots early.
"The majority of observers who supervised them share the opinion that the process did not provide sufficient guarantees for neutrality and transparency," the statement said.

Almost all the opposition parties complained after last Thursday's poll of irregularities in the election. The authorities hoped the election would end more than five years of violence they blame on Moslem fundamentalists.

But The statement said the "observers were impressed by the material and logistical preparation for the election, the professionalism of members of the voting offices and the harmony in which the poll took place."

"However several political parties pointed out to observers the lack of information about the hours and itinaries of the 'caravans' and also the fact they were not allowed to accompany them," it added.
